meta.primary_text: Who are you actually talking to? With The CheqUp Method, your Health Coach has a name. They plan with you by message or call, alongside a UK Clinician who reviews your history and the WeightWatchers app.
meta.headline: Weight loss made simple with The CheqUp Method

approvals_pending.landing: Legal-approved landing page needed. meta.url is unset and the endcard url is ‘TBC’ on purpose: the url placeholder is a HOLD no approvals key clears, so the board can’t publish until someone sets the approved URL after every item below is signed off (compliance.py doesn’t read approvals_pending yet). Never /how-it-works.
approvals_pending.weightwatchers: WeightWatchers partner approval for the app mention. Confirm ‘included’ is true for every membership tier, and give WeightWatchers sight of the full script (its app sits next to an anti-automation joke).
approvals_pending.platform_line: ‘Made simple’ is also used by Oxford Online Pharmacy, My Health Needs UK and LloydsPharmacy (Meta, 8 Oct). Vicky’s line; flagged, not changed.
approvals_pending.proposition: ‘Your Health Coach has a name.’ Confirm every member has one named, individual Health Coach (not a rota or a shared inbox). The device shrinks ‘the team’ to ‘Team.’ (anonymity), not ‘shortly’ (time).
approvals_pending.comparative_claims: Legal question: the device implies a comparison with the category (other providers’ support is anonymous or automated). Before publication legal needs (a) evidence that the parodied behaviour is a real, typical category practice and (b) evidence of CheqUp’s own journey: a human Coach for every member, plans individually built, no auto-reply in the channels a member uses (site chat, onboarding emails, app nudges, the bundled WeightWatchers app). CAP 3.1, 3.3, 3.7; 3.33 if a rival becomes identifiable.
approvals_pending.coach_contact: Legal question, not a conclusion: does any part of the film imply a reply time or availability? If legal reads one, CheqUp must hold evidence of typical Coach first-contact and reply times (CAP 3.7; ruling A24-1264775). Also confirm exactly which contact modes exist (‘by message or call’; video?) and that Coaches are people, not automated.
approvals_pending.indirect_pom: Legal question: do the signals together read as a prescribing-pharmacy service (sign-up, ‘a UK Clinician’, ‘Eligibility criteria apply’, ‘Regulated by the CQC and GPhC’, the ‘Check my eligibility’ button)? ASA guidance: a consultation ad should not indicate that the likely outcome is a POM; A25-1305722 upheld POM promotion without a named medicine. ‘Eligibility’ is no longer spoken. Ask whether GPhC must appear in this legal line, and confirm a non-medication membership path exists that makes ‘eligibility’ accurate.
approvals_pending.clinician: ‘A UK Clinician reviews your history’: confirm a clinician reviews each member’s history (the line no longer says members talk to the clinician, or that the clinician ‘knows’ them).
approvals_pending.illustrative: The chats, the name Jo and Sue’s name are illustrative; the legal line says so.
approvals_pending.voices: The customer’s voice is synthetic (Chatterbox from a Kokoro-made reference; no real person cloned); she is a dramatised prospective customer, not a member or a testimonial. The Health Coach is never voiced by TTS: Coach chat bubbles are unvoiced and the spoken CheqUp lines are third-person announcer lines.
approvals_pending.broll_required: No fallback stills on purpose: every design-system photo shows smiling faces, which would cast a real model as the Coach, the Clinician or the customer. If a plate fails, the board errors (REPORT.md says which scene) instead of rendering a misleading still. For a layout-only draft, copy the board to the scratchpad and set src_locked on its media scenes.
approvals_pending.timing: Bot and Coach bubbles use fixed ‘at’ times set at least 0.45 s after each line’s estimated end (2.9 words/s). Re-set them after the PC voice pass if a read runs slower (the renderer has no ‘after_line’ yet).
approvals_pending.formats_16x9: 16x9 dropped until the renderer has a 16:9 chat layout, a -23 LUFS VOD master (render.mjs normalises to -14 LUFS) and a visible endcard URL, and the cut is re-timed to about 29.5 s. Live-action is the VOD route (Clearcast first).

scenes.broll: A white mug of tea and a phone lying face-down on the painted sill of a tall sash window in the front room of a Victorian terraced house on a bright morning. Beside them on the sill: a small fern in a terracotta pot and a folded pair of reading glasses. Beyond the glass: a quiet terraced street with black iron railings and a London plane tree turning gold. Below the sill: a white-painted radiator with a folded grey wool blanket on top. Low morning sun through the window throws crisp window-shaped patches of light across the sill and the wall. Vertical frame: the upper half is plain white painted wall and window frame, the mug and phone sit just below the centre, the radiator and oak floorboards fill the bottom. 50mm lens at f/5.6.
scenes.broll_brief: a mug of tea and a face-down phone on a sash-window sill (the UK Clinician beat, people-free)
scenes.motion: Steam rises slowly from the mug while the plane tree leaves move gently outside the window. The light stays steady. The camera pushes in very slowly.

scenes.headline: Included.
scenes.broll: Close, high-angle view of a woman's hands cooking a vegetable stir-fry in a black wok on a gas hob in a bright home kitchen at midday. Her right hand turns strips of red pepper, broccoli florets and sliced spring onion with a wooden spatula; her left hand tips in a handful of sugar snap peas from a small white bowl. Beside the hob: half a lime on a wooden board. Only her hands and forearms are in frame, a rolled-up cream knitted sleeve, short unpainted nails and a silver watch, a Black British woman in her forties. Sun from a window on the left lights the rising steam and throws crisp shadows across the worktop. Vertical frame: the upper half is plain sunlit white tiled splashback, the wok and hands sit just below the centre, the worktop edge fills the bottom. 50mm lens at f/8.
scenes.broll_brief: her hands cooking a vegetable stir-fry at midday (the WeightWatchers app beat)
scenes.motion: Steam rises slowly and the wooden spatula makes one slow turn through the vegetables. Fixed camera.
